Re: Appeal of denial for partial knee replacement  
CPT 27446  
Reference number: POC-CA1D31244E-60243

Dear Appeals Department:

I appeal the denial of prior authorization for my partial knee replacement, CPT 27446. The denial states that the submitted records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. The available clinical records directly address that reason and document prolonged symptoms, multiple conservative treatments, objective structural disease, and substantial functional impairment.

The records establish the following:

- I have experienced 14 months of progressive knee pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- I used NSAIDs for four months, with inadequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on April 21, 2026. It provided only four weeks of partial relief.
- I completed 16 supervised physical therapy visits over eight weeks, from May 17, 2026, through July 12, 2026. Therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, and the treatment course is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- MRI imaging dated June 15, 2026, shows full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medial disease.
- My pain causes major functional limitations. I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake three to four times every night because of pain.
- Examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
- The record documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a nonsmoker.

This is not a request based on failure of only one treatment. The records document medication treatment, injection treatment, and a completed supervised physical therapy program, together with persistent symptoms and severe objective disease. The therapy course was completed shortly before the denial, and the continued pain and functional limitations demonstrate that conservative treatment has not adequately controlled the condition.

I request that the denial be reversed and that authorization for CPT 27446 be approved. Please have the case reviewed by an orthopedic physician or other qualified clinician who is familiar with knee arthroplasty and the submitted MRI and treatment records. The treating surgeon is Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery.

The Florida Medicaid Orthopedic Services Coverage Policy that is publicly available provides general requirements for medically necessary orthopedic services and lists musculoskeletal surgery among covered orthopedic services. However, the specific payer-specific clinical review policy applied to this denial has not been identified or provided to me, and I am not quoting the plan’s policy. Please provide, as part of this appeal, the exact policy or clinical review criteria used for CPT 27446, including its title, policy number, version or effective date, the precise conservative-treatment requirement, and the clinical rationale for finding the submitted records insufficient.

Please also provide the complete utilization-review file, including the records reviewed, the reviewer’s credentials, and any criteria or checklist used in reaching the decision. If any additional documentation is required, please identify it specifically so it can be submitted promptly.

This appeal must be received by February 1, 2027, as stated in the adverse benefit determination. Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the appeal decision in writing.

Sincerely,

Taylor Alvarez  
Member ID: W131874845
